label: Constitutional Amendment A
t: Publish proposed amendments online, not in newspapers
what: The constitution now requires proposed amendments to be printed in a newspaper in every county for two months before the election. This amendment would instead require publication for the 60 days before the election in a manner set by state law. The accompanying statute would have the Lieutenant Governor post the full text on the Utah Public Notice Website and the Lieutenant Governor's website.
y: Proposed amendments are published for 60 days in a way set by law (online), not in county newspapers.
n: The two-month newspaper publication requirement stays.
pro: State Sen. Dan McCay, State Rep. Anthony Loubet

label: Constitutional Amendment B
t: 60% vote for citizen initiatives that raise taxes
what: Citizen initiatives that impose a new tax, expand an existing tax, raise a tax rate, or cut a property tax rate by less than current law would need at least 60% voter approval instead of a simple majority. Laws passed by the Legislature are not affected. If approved, it would apply to initiatives on the 2026 ballot.
y: Tax-raising citizen initiatives need 60% approval to pass.
n: Citizen initiatives continue to need a simple majority.
pro: Utah Taxpayers Association, State Sen. Lincoln Fillmore, State Reps. Jason Kyle and Jason Thompson
con: ACLU of Utah, League of Women Voters of Utah, Mormon Women for Ethical Government, Alliance for a Better Utah, Disability Law Center
